issues.legal_issue: Acquittals of some alleged participants do not prevent conviction of the remaining participants for acting as members of an unlawful assembly when the evidence firmly establishes that the assembly included at least five persons and the doubt concerns only the identity of some participants.
material_facts: Eighteen persons were alleged to have participated in an attack in which two people were killed.
The trial court acquitted eleven accused, and the High Court acquitted additional accused, leaving four appellants convicted.
The appellants admitted participating in the occurrence, and injuries on three of them corroborated their presence.

The courts found that the attack involved at least five assailants, relying on the victims' injuries, the manner of the attack, and the circumstances in which the attackers waited for and surrounded the victims.
The courts gave the acquitted accused the benefit of doubt about their individual participation, while finding the appellants' participation established.
issues.conclusion: The acquittals did not require the court to presume that fewer than five assailants took part. The appellants' convictions for murder with the aid of unlawful-assembly liability were affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, vicarious liability depends on proof beyond reasonable doubt that the accused participated in an unlawful assembly of at least five persons acting in pursuit of its common object; it does not depend on convicting the required number of named defendants. A finding that the total number of participants was at least five is distinct from doubt about the identity of particular participants, and acquitted persons' presumption of innocence does not automatically benefit convicted persons. The Court applied this distinction while discussing Yeshwant v. State of Maharashtra and Sukh Ram v. State of U.P., and distinguished the cases relied on by the appellants, including Krishna Govind Patil v. State of Maharashtra.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and convicted_participation_proved and assembly_size_at_least_five and identity_doubt_only

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.convicted_participation_proved: The evidence establishes beyond reasonable doubt that the convicted accused participated in the attack.
predicates.assembly_size_at_least_five: The evidence establishes that at least five persons participated in the attack.
predicates.identity_doubt_only: The doubt concerns which particular participants took part, rather than whether the total number of participants reached five.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal concerns accused whose participation is proved, the assembly is found to have had at least five members, and doubt relates only to some participants' identities, the vicarious conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A juvenile's eligibility for a youth-specific sentencing measure may be considered when the relevant age and circumstances are established, but when the issue is raised only after trial and appeal, the court may recommend remission rather than order that measure.
material_facts: One appellant was found to have been about fifteen years old at the time of trial.
The youth-specific sentencing issue was not raised before either the trial court or the High Court.
The appellant was said to have carried a lathi, but prosecution witnesses assigned him no specific act.
No previous participation in a similar case or previous conviction was shown.
By the time the Supreme Court considered the matter, the appellant had already undergone part of his sentence.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not alter the conviction or sentence, but recommended that the authorities remit the appellant's remaining sentence.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29 of the Uttar Pradesh Children Act, 1951 permitted a court, after inquiry and if it considered such treatment expedient, to commit a child who had committed an offence punishable with imprisonment to an approved school, subject to the statutory age limit. Because the issue was not raised in time for the courts below to conduct the necessary inquiry, the Supreme Court recommended remission of the remaining sentence instead.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and juvenile_at_trial and youth_sentencing_issue_raised_late and sentence_remaining

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction and sentence.
predicates.juvenile_at_trial: The accused was below the relevant age threshold when tried.
predicates.youth_sentencing_issue_raised_late: The accused's eligibility for youth-specific sentencing treatment was not raised before the lower courts.
predicates.sentence_remaining: The accused has not completed the sentence when the appeal is decided.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a person who was a juvenile at trial, the youth-sentencing issue was raised only late, and part of the sentence remains, remission of the remaining sentence is recommended.
